about: Newest first. Every deploy of a visible change adds one entry with a picture; see FEEDBACK.md. Every shipped study gets one too (backfilled ones carry "backfill": true).

entries.title: No more emoji buttons or cards pill
entries.line: The cards pill is gone and the hand of cards is always there. The driving mode buttons are little 3D vehicles, and the duplicate notebook button is removed.

entries.title: Driving controls are little 3D things
entries.line: The row of round effect buttons and the cards pill are gone while you drive. The jet and boost buttons are now a real rocket and a lightning bolt.

entries.title: A light and an arrow show Abbie where to go
entries.line: When a neighbour asks for help, the next place glows with a spotlight, and an arrow at the edge of the screen points to it if it is out of view. Take the object out of your backpack and the favour is said again while the camera flies toward the place.

entries.title: Just the one world
entries.line: The strip of old land and the little floating island behind Winchester are gone. Only the seven-hex board is left in the sky.

entries.title: Everything in the town answers a tap
entries.line: Tap a house, a tree, a lamp, a shop, the ducks, bub or the little pink car and it reacts: a knock, a bell, a bark, a shower of leaves.

entries.title: Water balloons that carry their type
entries.line: The balls are now water balloons that wobble and squash in your hand. Fire, water, cats and dogs and tie-dye each have their own balloon, and when you throw one it lands that effect where it hits.

entries.title: Leave drive mode any time, and never lose your car
entries.line: A round close button (and Escape) always stops driving. The plain drive now passes through houses, trees and bushes, and a pale outline shows your car where scenery would hide it.

entries.title: Abbie's own backpack
entries.line: Everyone now starts with Abbie's backpack: the bunny in grape stripes with a heart pocket, pink and gold straps, a rainbow lining and the rainbow bear notebook. She wears it everywhere.

entries.title: One glass bar along the top
entries.line: Time, weather, the hex glow and the world effects now share a single glass bar, on iPad and phone too.

entries.title: Slide around the map with WASD
entries.line: On the Winchester map, W, A, S and D (or the arrow keys) slide the view over the ground. Hold Shift to go faster.

entries.title: The Farm
entries.line: A farm for the kids to explore, with cows, horses, goats, pigs, alpacas, sheep, ducks and bunnies. Find eggs, say hi, and help the farmer.

entries.title: Winchester filled in from the model library
entries.line: Main Street now has markets, benches and lamps, yards have gardens, farm bits and mailboxes, the Common has trees and a fountain, and the baker, the gardener and the neighbour are finished characters.

entries.title: Pick up a toy car and turn it around
entries.line: The garage now frames every car. Hold one to lift it, turn it with a finger, then put it back or choose it.

entries.title: Unzip your backpack and look closely
entries.line: Spin the backpack, unzip each pocket, tap a thing to hold it up big with a note about it, then put it back.

entries.title: Real music on the coaster, and a tidy backpack
entries.line: The ride plays our produced Abbie's World track instead of the synth band. The backpack closes cleanly: charms hang back where they belong and no gold coins float inside.
entries.threadTitle: Dispatch: coaster music and backpack cleanup

entries.title: Backpack upgrades and a place browser
entries.line: The backpack now upgrades with stars: more pockets, a bigger keyring. The cards along the bottom of the town are replaced by arrows that browse the places.

entries.title: The carwash and your Moon Buggy
entries.line: Roll the grubby buggy through the carwash, get soaked, and it's yours. Dress it with toy animals and colours.
entries.threadTitle: Earn the buggy at the carwash

entries.title: Tap a town card to turn its hex
entries.line: Tapping a tile card in the town's hand flips it open with that hex turning live in 3D; drag to turn it. Look, don't edit: Winchester stays as it is.

entries.title: Fuel to collect while you drive
entries.line: Embers, water drops, pet treats and dye drops sit along the track. Drive through one and it goes into your backpack to charge an effect.

entries.title: World effects hover, and charge up
entries.line: The effect icons are little 3D things now, greyed out until you charge them with an item from your backpack. Then they glow, and you can drop them on the world.

entries.title: Dress the backpack by its parts
entries.line: The card slots are gone. Little glass dots sit on the backpack itself: tap one, or tap the part, and a small row of colours or shapes opens beside it. Tap one and it goes on.

entries.title: Pick your toy car
entries.line: A round button on the left swaps your toy car for the next one: racer, camper bus, roll-cage buggy, truck cab and more.

entries.title: Paint fireball and slot machine
entries.line: Paint balls now live on the top bar as a paint-splat fireball with a count. Press it to spin the slot machine: three in a line wins a whole handful, and you can spin once a minute.

entries.title: Models is a proper library now
entries.line: Every model we have on one shelf with big pictures: search, studies down the side, and filters for source, type, place and status. Tap one to turn it around.
entries.threadTitle: Make all models easy to browse

entries.title: Models is a proper library now
entries.line: Every model we have on one shelf with big pictures: search, studies down the side, and filters for source, type, place and status. Tap one to turn it around.
entries.threadTitle: Make all models easy to browse

entries.title: Car mode in the town, and a phone for Polaroids
entries.line: Car mode now runs in the real town: a looping track threaded between the houses, scenery to smash, ramps and boost pads, fire wheels when you have the charm, the real toy cars, and after you win the floppy disk a mini phone that takes Polaroids while you drive.

entries.title: Backpack and notebook on the left
entries.line: Abbie's backpack now sits on a glass bar on the left as a little 3D backpack, with her fluffy notebook under it. Her notebook holds her quests, written in pencil on yellow paper, and she can pick from seven fluffy covers.

entries.title: People in Winchester ask for help
entries.line: The baker, the teacher, the postie and friends now stand around town. Tap one and they ask a favour; say yes and it goes in your notebook, and the reward lands in your backpack.

entries.title: The town screen, tidied
entries.line: Drafted: one row along the top for the clock and the world effects (icons now, not cards), a glowing hex grid button, and the tile cards back in a hand along the bottom with the Paint card (tap a tile to fly to it). The old bottom bar is gone. The backpack and notebook bar on the left comes from the backpack thread.

entries.title: A sky behind Winchester, and the café door
entries.line: A soft sky now sits behind the town board and follows the clock, the season and the weather, and tapping the café on Main Street takes you inside.

entries.title: Coaster: real toy cars, fire wheels and the town clock
entries.line: Four free toy-car models from Printables now park in the coaster garage beside our own six. Win the Toy car charm to unlock fire wheels. Tap during the ride to bring up the clock, and night, clouds and rain light the ride.

entries.title: The charms light the way in
entries.line: Winchester opens in the dark with your backpack charms circling under a spotlight. When it's ready they fold into the backpack, the lights go out, and the town drops in.

entries.title: Winchester warms up quietly
entries.line: The town compiles its own shaders in the background so placing and walking don't hitch.

entries.title: Models open faster
entries.line: The model browser shows a quiet loading ring while a 3D model arrives, loads the next ones ahead, and the laser print effect is gone.

entries.title: The backpack floats out to dress up
entries.line: Tap the backpack on the weather instrument and it floats to the middle of the screen, with a card slot for its style, colour, pattern, pocket, straps and lining. Drop a card in a slot and it changes straight away.

entries.title: Tiles build themselves
entries.line: Drop a tile and it rolls in bare, then every tree, building and fence drops from the air, tumbles, hovers and snaps into place, all in about a second and a half. Accept in the card designer now prints the tile with a laser and signs it with a tick.

entries.title: World look: three looks, one switch
entries.line: Developer tools only: Storybook (the town's own), Sunday toon (the Ranch's original) and the new Comic ink, thick black cartoon outlines. Open /town?dev and use the World look box.

entries.title: A proper skate park
entries.line: The skate park by the coffee shop now has quarter pipes, a funbox, stairs with a rail, grind rails, a painted mural wall, lamps, cones and boards lying about.

entries.title: The coaster, in Winchester, with sound and slow motion
entries.line: Tap the coaster on the skate park by the café. Pick one of six toy cars (yes, a shopping cart), hear the theme play as you ride, and duck: a tennis ball nearly takes your helmet off in slow motion. Your ride photo waits at the finish.

entries.title: Paint the World in Winchester
entries.line: The Paint card and splat balls now work in the town too: get a handful, drag one onto the hexes and let go. The paint splats, and strange plants grow from it.

entries.title: World event cards in Abbie's Town
entries.line: Tap the little lightning button in the town to open the event cards: fireball, waterball, cats and dogs, tie-dye.

entries.title: The weather instrument in the town
entries.line: The chronograph now sits top left in Abbie's Town and the demo, with her backpack on it. Time of day dims the town, and weather and season are on the dial. Drafted: weather and season don't change the town yet.

entries.title: Aurora Mk 2 in 3D: eight ships
entries.line: Meshy turned all eight ship pictures into 3D models, and each one is mirrored so it is exactly symmetric. Spin each beside its picture and tell me which one to build out.

entries.title: Kart mode: the board becomes a racetrack
entries.line: Drive the jet cart round a looping track stencilled from the town's tiles: crash through cones and hay, bounce off benches, hit ramps and boost pads, and when you place a tile the track grows to include it.

entries.title: Fling your own paint
entries.line: Spending the Paint card now gives you a random handful of splat balls, big or small. Drag one from the right edge and let go: it flies, splats, and grows glowing plants, faster than before.

entries.title: Fireballs, water balloons, cats and dogs, tie-dye
entries.line: Four new world event cards: drop a fireball or a giant waterball, rain cats and dogs, or turn the whole world tie-dye with a sitar. Each lasts a day and nobody is hurt.

entries.title: Character Studio: the Meshy heroes
entries.line: The Meshy heroes are in the studio: the claymation adventurer, the plasticine inventor, the 80s action hero and the twelve astronauts (Commander, Engineer, Daddy, Abbie, Ani and the alien crewmate, each in two looks). Every move plays on all of them.

entries.title: Play world events from the toy box
entries.line: Open World events in the toy box: a column of event cards on the far right. Tap one to make it rain, snow, storm, fog, dawn, nightfall or paint fall.

entries.title: The Moon Mission starts at the bakery
entries.line: The Moon Mission now starts and launches from the French bakery on Main Street.

entries.title: World events are cards now
entries.line: Paint rain, storms, snow, rainbows, dawn, nightfall, fog, northern lights and the meteorite each get a collectible card, in a night-blue frame with a burst window and a WORLD EVENT banner so they never look like tile cards.

entries.title: Walk in at Grace's computer
entries.line: Abbie's World now opens in the dark. A desk lamp clicks on and Grace's computer glows, calling you to tap it and play her basement game while the shaders get ready. When it's ready, a popup lets you enter Winchester.

entries.title: A French bakery downtown
entries.line: A little French bakery with a croissant sign now stands on Main Street in Winchester, and it is where the Moon Mission starts.

entries.title: The Moon Mission in Winchester
entries.line: The Moon Mission now plays inside the Winchester map: the rocket launches from the café roof, space and the Moon are night scenes, and when you land the map comes back.

entries.title: The Effect Hunt: a jet shopping cart
entries.line: Ten effects are hidden around Winchester. Pick the hunt in the notebook, follow the laser beams, and drive Abbie, Ani and Daddy in a jetpack cart. Once found, an effect is yours forever on a 15 second cooldown.
entries.threadTitle: AW-STUDY-0057 - Effect hunt and jet cart

entries.title: Real charms on the backpack
entries.line: The tardigrade, heart, moon, rocket, star and floppy disk charms are now sculpted models made from their Midjourney pictures, and there is a toy car charm for the coaster.

entries.title: Abbie and Ani have tree houses
entries.line: Abbie's pink blossom tree house and Ani's violet moon tree house now stand in their backyards on the Winchester board, built from the iPad game art. The backpack is in the town too.

entries.title: Real astronauts on the Moon
entries.line: The Moon Mission crew are now the Meshy astronauts, and Abbie wears her backpack with her jingling charms on the Moon.

entries.title: A toy-car coaster at the skate park
entries.line: Zoom down onto the skate park, tap the little yellow car and ride a 30 second first-person coaster with a loop, a corkscrew and a jump. Catch ten stars and win the Toy car charm.

entries.title: Abbie wears her backpack
entries.line: Her charms swing and jingle wherever she is shown, and each one can live on the backpack or in her jewellery box. The floppy disk charm now comes from beating the word game.

entries.title: The school's coin is now a charm
entries.line: The gold coin on the school canopy is gone. Reaching the roof wins Abbie her Star charm, and getting onto the canopy is the memory.

entries.title: Aurora Mk 2 concept art
entries.line: Five rounds of concept art for the new family explorer: key art on the Moon, a design sheet, three makers side by side, a cutaway and the cockpit. Pick the one you like and it goes to Meshy.

entries.title: A Star charm for the school roof
entries.line: Getting onto the school roof now wins Abbie a Star charm for her backpack, with the golden jingle.

entries.title: Winchester, MA is one board of seven hexes
entries.line: Abbie's Town is now a single board of seven hexes on the real hills and ponds: the high school in the middle, Downtown, Ani's side and Abbie and Daddy's side around it.

entries.title: The demo: tour, town and missions
entries.line: Cartoon Abbie and Ani give a tour of Winchester, the strange scientist unfolds a launch pad from the café roof, then you place tiles and pick a mission.

entries.title: Charms map and jewellery box
entries.line: A chest of ten charms, locked cards that show a padlock where to earn them, and the mission board for the demo.

entries.title: Three launch consoles
entries.line: Chapter 1 now ends on the Moon. Daddy times the booster burns, Ani swaps the cows for veggies, Abbie lands us, then everyone gets a Polaroid. The moon base games move to Chapter 2.

entries.title: Mine moon cheese
entries.line: On the Moon there's a mining outpost with a kiosk. Break moon rocks: one in three hides a cheese, and three cheeses win a moon cheese charm for the backpack. Win as many as you like (two hang on the keychain).

entries.title: A properly made space suit
entries.line: The crew's suits now have panels, seals at every joint, a chest control plate, life-support pack with tanks, a gold-tint visor and helmet lamps. Before on the left, after on the right.

entries.title: A better-made backpack
entries.line: Abbie's backpack now looks sewn and zipped: real cloth and leather grain, stitching round every panel, zip teeth, padded straps, and shiny gold that catches the light.

entries.title: The Moon Mission starts in the town
entries.line: A black truck is parked on Main Street outside the coffee shop. Tap it and the Moon Mission begins right there in the town diorama.

entries.title: Your loved looks, built
entries.line: Ink and paper, Line art, Dusk mist, One-bit and the world orb are now real kits you can drag a slider on: the page turns to ink, the mist rolls in, the old screen dithers, and the orb opens into a new world.

entries.title: Texture Studio: cleaner brute paint
entries.line: The dark smudges on the brute's skin and clothes are gone from every look; the Saturday Action ink look is the clean one to start with.

entries.title: A card that paints the world
entries.line: Play the Paint the World card and coloured paint falls from the sky onto your board. It stays for a day of game time, and strange alien plants grow out of it.

entries.title: Characters drawn in pieces, and moving
entries.line: The mannequin drawn the way Spine and Rive games do it: SVG pieces on bones, joints that never gap, arms you can pull, and a jump with a real wind-up and squash. Six practice tries side by side, each one better.

entries.title: Light study: fourteen ways to light the world
entries.line: Golden hour, a café window shaft, a bare basement bulb, a hard-sun Moon base and a cosy Halloween dusk, all rebuilt live on our ranch. Pick the ones you love.

entries.title: Watercolour distance
entries.line: Pull back in Abbie's Town and the far world turns to wet watercolour. Downtown, Ani's side and Abbie and Daddy's side each paint their distance in their own colours.

entries.title: Games in Grace's basement
entries.line: A pocket game player on Grace's desk plays falling blocks in one-bit dither, and her DOS computer now has real games on disks: BLOCKS and DUSKBLADE, a sword-and-traps palace in our own style. Type GAMES.

entries.title: Your hero, rigged
entries.line: The flying hero you pasted is now cut into parts on a named skeleton with hair, belt and scarf as decorations, and it turns. A Unity-style export is included (not yet run in Unity).

entries.title: Walk into the café
entries.line: Step through the café's front doors and walk Abbie round the real room, day or night. Turn the jukebox on, find what the register is hiding, and try the old door behind the bar.

entries.title: Drawn by hand, 12 frames
entries.line: The brute fight has a pencil button: poses hold for two frames, the pen line redraws every drawing, and each hit freezes the picture a beat.

entries.title: Nine kinds of house
entries.line: The town's houses are now capes, bungalows, triple-deckers, colonials, split-levels, farmhouses, Victorians, Tudors and estates, in three tiers of wealth, with porches, fences, walls and mailboxes.

entries.title: Up the stairs into the café
entries.line: Leaving Grace's basement, by the door or at the end, now takes you up into the café. Daddy's call in the ending is written as a script that the Moon Mission will reuse.

entries.title: Male and female figures, pencil drawn
entries.line: Two mannequins, a woman and a man, posed in a heroic leap and a run, then drawn by the code pencil with form hatching. The pose now drives the drawing.

entries.title: A code pencil, tried end to end
entries.line: We drew the leaping figure again with an emulated pencil: pressure, tapered ends, hand wobble and paper grain. The Midjourney hero steps wait on your signed-in Chrome.

entries.title: Moon Mission: low-poly isometric view and the four Moon base games
entries.line: The Moon Mission now plays from above in a low-poly isometric view, and after landing there are four more games: wire the airlock door, zap the gem bugs in the habitat, hum back the Star Child's song, and drive the buggy home. Nobody can fail; mistakes only cost a moment. Stand-in figures until the Meshy heroes arrive.
entries.threadTitle: AW-STUDY-0044 - Why Our Drawing Is Weak

entries.title: Why our drawing is weak
entries.line: We traced a Midjourney sketch four ways and found the trace is fine: the weakness is redrawing instead of keeping the picture's line. A puppet cut from the traced lines keeps its feel when it moves.
entries.threadTitle: AW-STUDY-0044 - Why Our Drawing Is Weak

entries.title: Winchester as three dioramas
entries.line: Downtown, Ani's side, and Abbie and Daddy's side are now three little worlds you can hold: the real hills and ponds squeezed small, the places pushed together and built big, each with its own light and its own pulled-back view. /town opens on them.

entries.title: Character Studio: only Meshy figures
entries.line: The studio now plays every move on the two Meshy brutes and nothing else; the wooden mannequins, game figure and kids are gone from the cast. New Meshy heroes join once they are rigged.

entries.title: Moon Mission: the black truck, the rocket port and the pink ship, in the town
entries.line: Moon Mission Part 1 now plays in the 3D world. A black truck pulls up at the coffee shop, you accept, a huge rocket port lands and the pink ship falls right after. Then the kitchen, the tree house, launch, the Moon landing and the Moon base, all low-poly scenes. Stand-in figures until the Meshy heroes arrive.

entries.title: Abbie's Science Adventure
entries.line: Our first 2D game: shader water, rigged SVG cells and the lens on every body. The microbe kit and lens pond are shared for the next 2D game.

entries.title: Switching boards
entries.line: Pull back and your boards are hexes of a bigger board: tap one to land in it, or tap the dashed hex to start a new one. Try three ways in a playable prototype.

entries.title: Winchester as seven hexes
entries.line: Press the hex button and the town shows as seven hexes in one greater hex, carved into three regions of about a third each: Downtown, Ani's side, and Abbie and Daddy's side.

entries.title: Character Studio: real figures, real motion, scored
entries.line: Every move now plays on figures we already trust: the game figure, Young Daddy and the girl from Grace's basement. Each move was scored for weight, timing and footwork beside a real clip; 11 stiff ones were cut and 8 swapped for real game animation. The new Scores room shows every one before and after.

entries.title: Abbie's Town: home, treehouses and a splash pad
entries.line: Abbie's house and Ani's house now stand in the town, each with a treehouse in the backyard, and Daddy's hideaway door is in the grass under Abbie's. Horn Pond has a splash pad on the shore.

entries.title: Abbie's Town through the years
entries.line: Press the clock and the town grows from the first farmhouses in 1700, with the railway arriving in 1835. Press the map and the real streets and buildings of Winchester lie over the land, so you can see how it lines up.

entries.title: Backpack charms up close
entries.line: Tap a charm on Abbie's backpack and the camera comes in close while it turns to face you; swipe for the next. Decorate the bag with cards: tap a part, then drop a card on it. The first charm is a tardigrade, won in the cell game.

entries.title: Abbie's backpack
entries.line: Her pocket is now a backpack. Tap it and it opens all the way, like a clamshell, with her things in both halves. Pick one of ten styles, change five facets, and earn a charm for every quest; the first ones come from Daddy's core memories.

entries.title: Character Studio: four new characters
entries.line: The claymation adventurer, the plasticine inventor, the stick man and the 80s action hero from Midjourney are now 3D characters that play every move. The new Cast room shows each one beside its picture.

entries.title: Texture Studio: a painted, Arcane-style light
entries.line: The Texture Studio's light button now has a fifth light, Painted Brush: brush-broken shadows, purple shade, a teal rim and broken ink. There's also an "As modelled" look that shows the original paint, ready for the Meshy-textured brutes.

entries.title: Inspiring Shaders: pick the looks you love
entries.line: Fourteen game looks rebuilt live on our mannequin, brute and ranch, starting with the Arcane-inspired Painted Brush beside Sunday Toon. Tap Love it, Maybe or Not for us on each, and add a note.

entries.title: The puppet does all 50 Character Studio moves
entries.line: Tap the first card under the puppet to swap to the Character Studio's 50 moves, from cozy life to fighting to dance, played by the wooden mannequin from the side.

entries.title: Character Studio: real motion
entries.line: The wooden mannequin moves with real motion capture: 50 moves from every kind of game, filmed with depth, haze and a golden-hour crowd. Try four looks (clay, plasticine, stick man, 80s action), pick the doll up, and the 2D puppet sits next door.

entries.title: Abbie's Town
entries.line: A small, charming town on the real hills and lakes of Winchester at true scale. The coffee shop, Comella's, Frozen Hoagies, Muraco, Leonard Field, Ginn Field and Horn Pond are where they are, Launch and New Nova sit off the map, and tapping the heart makes the coffee shop Abbie's.

entries.title: Texture Studio: dress the heroes
entries.line: Pick a brute and one of four looks (whimsical clay, Stick Man storybook, Wallace and Gromit plasticine, 80s cartoon action). Paint him with a brush or fill a whole part, then watch all four heroes walk from a distance.

entries.title: Every new thing, in one place
entries.line: Later and Dismiss now sit right under the picture, with a close button so you never have to choose. "+ more" and History open a viewer of every update, unread and read, each linking to its study.

entries.title: The puppet walks like a person now
entries.line: The mannequin's feet stay planted on a floor that slides by, its hips rise and fall with each step, and its arms swing and trail behind. One dial takes it from a walk to a jog to a run.

entries.title: Spaceship games study
entries.line: How Star Citizen, Starfield and EVE design their ships, all 27 space games in the Oracle, the rules Abbie's World adopts, and a white-box ship you can land, board and fly.

entries.title: What each study drew on
entries.line: Every study now has a Context card on the right: the Oracle games it consulted, the dev and design blogs, the tutorials and our own canon. Where nothing was written down it says so.

entries.title: Faces that feel
entries.line: A toy with 18 feelings, from joy to sleepy, as a 3D face, a painted face and a faceless wooden body. Type a line and it says it with the right face. Plus how 40 of your games do faces.

entries.title: Moon base: the dome, the tower and real crater rocks
entries.line: The main dome and the comms tower, built from your Midjourney pictures, plus a new crater rim and boulder set drawn as rocks only. Each sits beside its picture, and you can spin it.

entries.title: The wooden mannequin, as a puppet
entries.line: Drag any joint of the blue-graphite mannequin and it follows; pull the hips down and it crouches with its feet planted. Set keys on the strip, or tap one of 18 moves from waving to a backflip.

entries.title: A founding city on hexes
entries.line: A new place found by simulation: a limestone headland with a spring and a calm bay. The big tile splits into 217 hex blocks and a town grows on them. Play the years, zone a block, and ask the steward how the town is doing.

entries.title: Moon Mission: the storyboard for tonight
entries.line: The family Moon game, planned for the big TV: 13 frames from the kitchen to the Moon base pad, everyone's jobs, live Houston on the radio, white suits on Earth and dark mode on the Moon.

entries.title: Moon base kit, rebuilt from your Midjourney picks
entries.line: 18 of the 20 Moon base pieces rebuilt to match their Midjourney pictures: chunky white modules in dark frames with warm orange windows. Each card shows the picture, the model you can spin, Abbie's view and the first try.

entries.title: The school, redone at dusk
entries.line: The school jump's school matches the key art now: a low golden sun, tree shadows on the brick, a slate roof edge, a boiler chimney, a flag, swings and hopscotch. It's all drawn in the new Sunday Toon look.

entries.title: Young Daddy, bub and the basement girl, rebuilt
entries.line: The kids and the dog in Daddy's memory places are now smooth, skinned figures with real cloth, hair and fur, so the storybook light makes their ears glow and their outlines shine. See them before and after.

entries.title: Grace's basement has an ending
entries.line: Run the gold disk and the basement warms up. Daddy calls down, Abbie climbs back to the café with his memory in her pocket, and the old set switches off. Every coin is a piece of that memory; find all ten to see it whole.

entries.title: The school jump, game ready
entries.line: Climbing works now: tap a hold and the hand that can reach it goes there. A new brick school at golden dusk, bub as a real black lab, young Daddy with arms and legs that climb, and station wagons that sweep the wall.

entries.title: Notes in every study
entries.line: Studies now show which ones are new to you. Each study has a Notes panel on the right: keep notes, send them to the study, or ask for a review. Details links the live page, its artifacts and the next study in the group.

entries.title: Feet on the stairs
entries.line: In Grace's basement the girl now steps down each stair, with her feet on the treads instead of through them. And if you go back up, "I have to know" brings you back to the start to choose again.

entries.title: Moon base kit: 20 pieces to walk through
entries.line: The first 20 of 200 pieces for the Moon shooter: hatch doors with light rings, oxygen canisters, gauges, bunks, a jump pad and more. Spin each one and see it from Abbie's eye height.

entries.title: Storybook light
entries.line: Your animated-film picture, rebuilt as live light: soft wrap light, warm rim, glowing ears and cheeks, green haze, round background blur and glow. Slide to compare with plain three.js and switch each part on or off.

entries.title: The family cast
entries.line: Everyone in Daddy's memory places, then and now, each with a storybook sheet and designed voices. Tap a voice, tick the one that sounds right, and send your picks.

entries.title: The school jump: chalk targets and a secret
entries.line: Hold and let go to throw: hit the two chalk targets and bub wants it further, then the third one sails onto the roof. The big jump is your choice now, and there is a secret ending if you dawdle.

entries.title: Brute Fight
entries.line: Two painted brutes brawl in a ranch ring. They fight on their own until you touch the screen, then you're the red one: jab, heavy, uppercut and the two-fisted hammer.

entries.title: The school jump, at golden dusk
entries.line: Walk your dog, throw the ball until it lands on the roof, then climb the long wall side-on, one hand at a time. Slow station wagons sweep the roof with their lights. Hide behind the two big walls, because getting caught burns.

entries.title: Grace's basement, warmed up
entries.line: The basement now warms up like an old TV. A little lamp shows you the switches, and the girl has a proper kid's face. She walks carefully down the stairs, and her thoughts appear at the bottom in pixel letters with > choices. Every memory coin gets the golden reward.

entries.title: Why the brute came out boxy
entries.line: The Bruiser study's post-mortem: his picture is turned about 23 degrees, every hand-built body was too thin front to back, and the five rules that fix it.

entries.title: The café tells its story
entries.line: A pin board behind the bar shows who comes here: photo strips, a little drawing, a moon postcard and a lost mitten. A tip jar sits by the till, and the photo booth buttons bounce and glow when you pick.

entries.title: The café photo booth
entries.line: Step into the photo booth with a friend. The booth shows a pose, the bulbs count down, strike it before the flash. After four flashes your strip drops out of the slot.

entries.title: The café, built
entries.line: Your dance-party café is built, low poly, with every piece weighed like the real thing. The bar is shorter now, a cash register hides a brass key, and an old door behind the bar leads somewhere secret.

entries.title: Abbie's pocket
entries.line: Things Abbie picks up go in her pocket on the top bubble, and she says what she thinks in her own small voice. The first thing to find is the café's brass key.

entries.title: Tap cards on the right
entries.line: Tap a building and its card waits on the far right without covering it. If it would, the view slides over. One short line, with the whole picture.

entries.title: The school jump
entries.line: Climb the old school's wall at dusk, hand over hand, then sneak across the roof past the headlights. Toss all 31 tennis balls down to your dog, hang-drop to the canopy and find a gold memory coin.

entries.title: Grace's basement, for real
entries.line: The basement starts dark: find the right switches (there are three). Then do Grace's list on her clipboard: plug the computer in, wash and dry the screen, switch it on and put in a disk. It runs real DOS now, and every gold coin is one of Daddy's memories.

entries.title: Pull a tile off its card
entries.line: Every card's tile is ready before you touch it. Drag a card onto the board and it rolls like a die into place. Tap a card to turn it over and make the tile yours; Accept prints it.

entries.title: The body, Gray's Anatomy deep
entries.line: The Bodies study now has a real skeleton and the muscles front, side and back, drawn from where Gray's Anatomy says each one attaches. Tap a muscle to read it. Joints, fat, measurements and the modelers' checklist are there too.

entries.title: Grace's basement
entries.line: Under the café is Aunt Grace's basement. Turn on the light, walk down the stairs and sit at her 1986 computer. Play KEYSTORM, try her disks, and find the ten gold coins.

entries.title: Welcome to Abbie’s World
entries.line: New players meet a tour guide: take the grand tour (the world builds itself, then a narrated tour of the live ranch), get a few chalk tips, or just play. Call it back any time from the toy box: Welcome tour.

entries.title: See every cent of your magic
entries.line: Signed in, your account now has a billing page: every talk, build and safety check, what it cost, and what's left this month. Support now comes in $5, $45 or $80 a month, almost all of it back as magic. The Kickstarter is gone.

entries.title: New things wait for you
entries.line: Each new thing now stays until you dismiss it. Dismiss shows the next one, Later keeps them all, and every one waits under Notices in Profile and settings.

entries.title: A front door for Abbie's World
entries.line: abbies.world now opens on a front door: what Abbie's World is, how it works, the PG promise, Play and Sign in, and support from $5 a month. Your home-screen app still goes straight to the ranch.

entries.title: Models fit on one screen
entries.line: Each model now fits on one screen: a hero bar with its name, the picture and the model side by side, and your feedback in its own panel on the right that you can hide. A menu on the left folds away. Profile and settings now open from your avatar, with 20 styles that change the whole app, and Studies has a home page.

entries.title: Hand cards show each place's cartoon
entries.line: Your hand cards now show the cartoon of each place in clean cel shading with ink lines: the barn and silo, the kitchen garden, a wildflower meadow with a bee skep, and the moon dome. Tap anything in the world and its card opens right beside it.

entries.title: Clouds over the ranch
entries.line: Clouds now sail low over the tiles, about 20 m up, and their shadows slide across the fields beneath them.

entries.title: Cards in clean cel shading
entries.line: The cards dropped the fake wood, brass and parchment. Every card now shows the real in-game model, cel-shaded with ink lines, in a flat frame with a quiet pattern for its place: barn boards on the ranch, sprout rows in the garden, flowers in the meadow, stars on the moon. Any card that isn't ready says PRELIMINARY · idea only.

entries.title: All the models, and Game mode
entries.line: See them all shows every model as a small card: the picture in its frame and the model beside it. Switch between one at a time and all at once. The gear now has App and Game: Game puts the page under the sky with seven styles, from Gallery to Candy party.

entries.title: Models come alive
entries.line: Your picture and its words sit together in one frame, and the model stands free beside it, printing itself in with a half-second laser. Labels and names are in Title Case, and Reject, Chat and Keep sit right under the pair.

entries.title: The Moon from Abbie's story
entries.line: The Moon is grey-blue now, with craters you can see, rocks thrown out round their rims, and tracks that stay in the dust. A glass dome with an orange band, a charcoal moon buggy that drives out to the geology field, and something new: a dark meteorite in a fresh crater, glowing cyan like a slow heartbeat.

entries.title: Models get the new look
entries.line: Model pages are simpler: AW in the corner, wordless counters, and your picture and the 3D model the same size. Numbered points show what matters on your picture and whether the model gets each one right. Reject, Chat (talk or type) and Keep sit under your right thumb. The gear switches between Default, Rome and Efficient, and the cart asks for more, with a camera. Every order starts as concept art.

entries.title: Weather you can watch coming
entries.line: Weather now arrives in fronts: the wind picks up, clouds gather and the animals settle before the rain, then the sky breaks up as it clears. Soft clouds float around your ranch and their shadows drift across the fields. Storms grey the sky, dim the sun and light the lamps, and a gentle flash brings thunder. The light is new too: a paper sky by day, a gold sunset, an ink-blue moonlit night with lamps that come on one by one at dusk, and Earthshine with lit windows on the Moon at night.

entries.title: Model pages are one review row
entries.line: Each model page is now your picture, the 3D model, and your notes with Reject, Adjust and Accept on the right. Name and score sit above, details below. Your verdict comes straight to Claude.

entries.title: Anyone can sign in and play
entries.line: Sign in is in the toy box now. Anyone can sign in with Google and play the ranch as their own copy, and their worlds follow them to any device. It's free, and we ask nothing of them. Talking to the Computer needs a sign-in, and everyone's AI spending has a cap: $1 a person, $100 for all players together, and $1000 for you.

entries.title: The world stays in view
entries.line: Opening a panel no longer dims or blurs the ranch, the teleport map floats over the world on a glass tray, and teleporting is a sparkle on the pad instead of a white-out.

entries.title: A glass chronograph for your ranch
entries.line: Time of day, pause, speed, weather and season are back in one glass dial at the top. Pin any dial you like, such as friends on the way or hungry animals, and keep your own to-dos there. The ranch suggests dials, and you can pin them or wave them off. The cards in your hand now have proper card faces.

entries.title: A soft ring, not a box
entries.line: Tap a building and a warm ring now glows on the ground around it, instead of the red debug box. Only you see the ring: the people on the ranch and the voice see just the ranch.

entries.title: The voice gets game sense
entries.line: Ask the voice for something that fights the game, like a timer floating in the sky, and it suggests a better version first (a bell that rings faster) and asks. Say no and it does it your way. A giant monkey stomping the town? You get it, and the townsfolk run and grumble.

entries.title: The world, edge to edge
entries.line: The sandbox lost its toolbar and side panel. Three glass toys remain: a sun dial at the top (tap to pause, hold for time and weather), your tile cards at the bottom, and a toy box with everything else. No more haze over the world. Classic layout is in the toy box.

entries.title: Ranch cards you can hold
entries.line: Open a pack of 15 Ranch cards made from the game's animals and buildings. Tilt them in the light, browse the binder, and print the whole set at studio quality. Settings, Studies, Cards.

entries.title: A rebuilt ranch
entries.line: Every building, animal, tree, prop and plant on the ranch was redrawn as concept art and rebuilt from it. The pen sheds, the cows and the goats are all new.

entries.title: Pick the Computer's voice
entries.line: Settings → Voice opens Live voice: choose OpenAI or ElevenLabs, the voice, speed, personality, reply length and how long it waits for little ones. Safety stays locked.

entries.title: School Jump: Game-Ready
entries.line: The school jump made game ready: the climb fixed, a full UX pass, and every model rebuilt as a hero low-poly recipe that the next memory game can reuse.

entries.title: Turnaround Hero
entries.line: Applies the bruiser method to a second figure: turnaround, depth ruler, anatomy base, planes.

entries.title: Moon Heroes
entries.line: One faceted body set, PG and true to shape, that every hero and the gear kit fit.

entries.title: Space Mail
entries.line: A whole mini game designed from our identity; waiting on your go to build it.

entries.title: Paper warrior
entries.line: Set the parts-first rule: each piece is modelled and fitted on its own.

entries.title: The voice runs the whole app
entries.line: The Computer now knows the ranch, its animals and the other worlds. Ask for a real barn, more goats, winter, a new tile or the moon base, and it does it.

entries.title: A sound library
entries.line: 450 sounds for the ranch and beyond, picked and levelled by the sound engineer. Open Sounds from Settings to browse them; they start playing once storage is switched on.

entries.title: Talk to the world
entries.line: Tap the microphone and just say what you want: the Computer builds it as you talk. It only plays the game, and it keeps things PG.

entries.title: The workshop
entries.line: Concept art and models fly in as they're made. Tap the factory button to see every job, its progress and the machines.

entries.title: Updates and feedback from your phone
entries.line: This card shows up when a new version is ready. Tap the speech bubble to send Claude a picture and a note.

entries.title: Paper helmet
entries.line: Made "same camera before and after" a rule for every study.

entries.title: Atelier pack
entries.line: Its trees, rocks and props replaced the Ranch’s old models in the game.
